messages:
maya: Quick design idea — introduce a per-route `consent_tier` that drives both sampling keys and telemetry visibility. goal: make inspect/replay safe by default and give ops a short TTL breakglass for debugging. sketch below.

maya: problem we're trying to solve: some routes (support chat, health checks) can carry PII but we still need useful telemetry and occasional replay for incidents. currently we either redact everything or leak too much.

tom: +1 on the tiering. question: how do we keep sampled traces stable across salt rotations? replays need the same sample selection.

maya: thinking "stable_hash_v2" keyed by route id + client_id_prefix, with salt rotation metadata embedded in the sample_key. we also store the salt version in the sample row for re-eval.

sasha: nit: storing client_id_prefix might itself be PII. we should only keep a deterministic truncated hash (first 12 hex) so we can bucket but not reverse. also ensure HMAC w/ KMS.

maya: agreed — HMAC(KMS) + truncate. ie: sample_key = hmac_kms(route||client_prefix||salt)[:12]  -> stable but not reversible.

liz: console UX: we'll need a per-route toggle: "Inspect allowed (ephemeral)" with TTL selector (default 5m). On the dashboard show columns: consent_tier, inspect_ttl, sampled_rate, last_salt_rotate. we should hide raw payloads unless user clicks 'reveal' and we force MFA + audit log.

andre: ops concerns: breakglass must require RBAC + two-person approval for >10m TTL. Also reveal flow must push an immutable audit entry to the central audit stream with who, why, and KMS unwrap event id.

maya: example config sketch:

```yaml
routes:
  - id: customer-chat
    consent_tier: explicit   # explicit | implied | none
    telemetry:
      sample_rate: 0.02
      sample_key: "stable_hash_v2"
      inspect_ttl: 300   # seconds, ephemeral reveal TTL
      reveal_policy: "mfa+audit"
```

tom: how does sampling interact with quota billing? if we hash-only a prefix for sampling, do we still bill full tokens? we need to keep cost metrics accurate.

maya: sampling is orthogonal to billing. billing uses token counts from the request metadata (we already emit token_count). telemetry rows reference the billing id but we never persist full prompt unless consent_tier==explicit AND reveal was used.

sasha: edge-case: concatenated prompts (system + user) — some PII in system tokens. we should expose a per-model sanitizer pipeline that runs before telemetry decision: tag tokens as "sensitive" and if >threshold then force consent_tier->none unless route overrides.

andre: rollout plan idea: start with read-only console fields + sampling_key inference for 2 weeks, then enable ephemeral reveal behind a feature flag for SREs only. monitor: reveal_count, reveal_latency, audit_failures.

liz: dashboard metric names: telemetry.inspect_reveals, telemetry.reveal_approvals, telemetry.reveal_denials, telemetry.sampled_rows_by_tier. add a CSV export for audits.

maya: one more subtlety: backfills/analytics may need hashed buckets stable across salt rotations. we add salt_version to rows and a migration helper that maps old buckets to new when necessary.

tom: SGTM. can we land a minimal RFC with the config sample + UX mock + ops checklist? i'll volunteer to write the sampling/keying section.

maya: thanks — i'll draft RFC. action items: (1) tom: write hashing/key rotation section, (2) liz: mockups for inspect toggle & reveal flow, (3) andre: ops runbook for breakglass & audit retention, (4) sasha: sanitizer rules proposal.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: note: feature-flag scaffolding created in staging, toggle: `telemetry.ephemeral_reveal` set to off by default.

liz: tagging for docs: please cc @devex once RFC draft is ready so we can update console help text.

maya: OK — aiming to post RFC by EOD Thurs. ping me here if you want to pair on sections. :thumbsup:

andre: small security ask: add a unit test that asserts no full_prompt rows are ever written for consent_tier != explicit.

sasha: will add sanitizer integration tests.

tom: LGTM on approach, leaving bikeshedding for RFC.

maya: thanks all.
